headline: No documented shared channel or overlapping write surface; only low-confidence interaction risks remain, with B's allowlisted egress the main asymmetry.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a non-runnable open-source collection with no I/O surfaces or shared channel, while profile B also shows no shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge. Without a communication path, B cannot inject into A or vice versa in the documented pair.
conditions: IF an orchestrator adds a shared clipboard, filesystem, or message queue between the agents, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Do not route raw outputs from one agent into the other's prompt.
Add provenance labels if a bridge is later introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile lists touched data classes, and neither exposes a shared workspace or filesystem. A has network_egress none; B has allowlisted egress, but with no documented sensitive data flow between them, leakage is not evidenced in this pair.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage becomes possible.
IF B is granted access to sensitive inputs and its allowlist includes an external API, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Review B's allowlist before enabling new destinations.
Disable file-sharing between the agents unless required.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no documented write surfaces or concurrency model, and B likewise shows no filesystem, git, or database write capability. With no overlapping mutable resource, there is no plausible capability conflict in the documented profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or mutable service, conflict risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Do not grant shared write access.
If writes are added, assign separate directories or accounts.
Introduce locking before any shared mutable resource is enabled.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a static collection and not runnable, so it cannot generate operational outputs for B to trust. B is a scientific-research agent, but with no documented input pipeline from A, the cascade pathway is only hypothetical and requires unusual orchestration.
conditions: IF an orchestrator starts feeding A's text into B as authoritative input, cascading error becomes possible.
mitigations: Do not use A as an upstream source of facts for B.
Require human review before B acts on any imported text.
Label A's content as untrusted reference material.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent, and both profiles show empty data_classes_touched. The pair therefore has no evidenced compliance mismatch to assess.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, compliance review is required.
mitigations: Check residency and retention settings if regulated data is introduced.
Avoid routing regulated data through undocumented agents.
